name: יוּשַׁב חֶסֶד
gloss: kindness is brought back; or kindness will be returned
summary: A son of Zerubbabel, of David's line, the last named of the five sons born after the return from Babylon. The name is a clause: יוּשַׁב, the hophal of שׁוּב “be brought back, be returned” (as Gen 43:12, the money “brought back” in the sacks), and חֶסֶד “kindness”. A son of the governor of the returned exiles named “kindness is brought back” matches the confession of that generation, that God “has extended חֶסֶד to us before the kings of Persia” (Ezr 9:9), and the promise that Yahweh's חֶסֶד would not depart from David's seed (2Sa 7:15); scripture does not explain the name itself.

evidence.note: Sons of Zerubbabel: “Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, יוּשַׁב חֶסֶד, five.”
“The money that was brought back (הַמּוּשָׁב) in the mouth of your sacks”: the hophal of שׁוּב.
“Our God has not forsaken us in our bondage, but has extended חֶסֶד to us before the kings of Persia.”
“My חֶסֶד shall not depart from him.”

note: The first element is from the root שׁוּב (entry shuv); the name is filed here under its noun. Its tokens are counted by BDB under the noun חֶסֶד (h.ed.ab) as well as v.bn.ak. The hophal reading of יוּשַׁב is the plain one; a qal passive would mean the same.
